### `nv_set_group_policy_mode`

| | |
|---|---|
| **Toolset** | `policy_write` (write) |
| **Endpoints** | `PATCH /v1/group/{name}` |
| **Annotations** | `readOnlyHint=False, destructiveHint=False, idempotentHint=True, openWorldHint=True` (`MUTATING_IDEMPOTENT`) |
| **Returns** | `WriteOutcome` |
| **SPEC §6.2 class** | Reversible config change — the mode can be set back, so `destructiveHint=False` even though `Protect` starts blocking. |

> **ALREADY IMPLEMENTED.** Exists in
> `reference/src/neuvector_mcp/tools/policy_write.py`, copied verbatim in Phase
> 0. Rule N3: **match the existing code exactly.** Transcription follows.

**Arguments**

| Name | Type | Default | Description (verbatim into `Field(description=...)`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `group_name` | `str` (min_length=1) | — | Group name, e.g. 'nv.api.prod'. |
| `mode` | `Literal["Discover", "Monitor", "Protect"]` | — | Discover learns behaviour, Monitor alerts, Protect blocks. |
| `confirm` | `str \| None` | `None` | Confirmation token from the plan returned by the first call. Omit on the first call to preview the change. |

**Query mapping**

| Argument | Controller parameter |
|---|---|
| `group_name` | path segment `{name}` |
| `mode` | JSON body `config.policy_mode` |

**Docstring (already in the file — do not reword)**

```
Change the policy mode of one group.

Moving a group to Protect starts BLOCKING traffic and process activity
that the learned policy does not allow. Preview first: call without
'confirm', read the returned plan, then call again with the token.

Calls PATCH /v1/group/{name} with {"config": {"name":..., "policy_mode":...}}.
```

**Body (already in the file — reproduced for reference only)**

```python
app = app_context(ctx)
payload: dict[str, Any] = {
    "config": {"name": group_name, "policy_mode": mode}
}
namespace = group_name.split(".")[-1] if group_name.startswith("nv.") else None

plan = authorise_write(
    app.settings,
    operation="nv_set_group_policy_mode",
    toolset="policy_write",
    target=group_name,
    effect=(
        f"Set policy mode of group {group_name!r} to {mode}."
        + (
            " Traffic and process activity outside the learned policy will be "
            "blocked immediately."
            if mode == "Protect"
            else ""
        )
    ),
    payload=payload,
    confirm=confirm,
    namespace=namespace,
)
if plan is not None:
    return plan

response = await app.client.request(
    "PATCH", f"/v1/group/{group_name}", json=payload
)
return WriteOutcome(
    status="applied",
    operation="nv_set_group_policy_mode",
    target=group_name,
    effect=f"policy_mode of {group_name} set to {mode}",
    payload=payload,
    controller_response=response if isinstance(response, dict) else {},
)

all three fail the same way: the controller answers 200 and changes
nothing, so an operator reads "applied" and believes enforcement is on

   /v1/service/config.

2. Mode moves must be adjacent. Discover -> Protect in one call is
   dropped. The new neuvector_mcp/modes.py reads the current modes with
   GET /v1/service, walks the ladder a rung at a time, and reads the
   services back afterwards -- reporting applied only for what the
   controller actually holds, and raising UpstreamError naming the real
   state when something did not land. A service already at the target
   contributes no step, so re-applying Protect never dips through Monitor.

3. The confirm token did not bind the dimension. scope selected the route
   and never entered the hashed payload, so all three scopes produced the

discard-a-two-rung-jump behaviour -- a respond(200, json={}) mock cannot
catch any of this. The two tests that encoded the scope-to-route model are

deliberate: the only scope value that did anything was the default, and a

All three defects were measured against the live 5.6.0 controller on 2026-07-31 by direct `X-Auth-Apikey` calls from inside the neuvector-mcp pod, and all three fail the same way: **the controller answers 200 and changes nothing**, so an operator reads `status: "applied"` and believes enforcement is active when it is not.

## What was broken

**1. The dimension is chosen by the payload field, not by the route.**
`RESTServiceBatchConfig` has five fields, not four — Appendix B omitted `profile_mode`. Measured route behaviour: `/v1/service/config` works, `/v1/service/config/network` honours only `policy_mode`, and `/v1/service/config/profile` is **inert on every field**. So `scope='profile'` never did anything, and because the tool exposed no `profile_mode` argument, **no tool in 1.1.0 could set process/file enforcement at all** (`nv_update_process_profile` only has entries / `alert_disabled` / `hash_enabled`).

**2. Mode moves must be adjacent.** `Discover → Protect` in one call is accepted and discarded. The ladder is `Discover → Monitor → Protect`.

**3. The confirm token did not bind the dimension.** `scope` selected the route and never entered the hashed payload, so all three scopes previewed to the identical token — a plan previewed as `profile` could be confirmed as `network`.

## What this does

- Adds `profile_mode`; drops `scope` and `_SERVICE_MODE_PATHS`; everything goes to `PATCH /v1/service/config`. Defect 3 disappears as a consequence — the dimension is now part of the hashed payload.
- New `src/neuvector_mcp/modes.py` owns the ladder. After the guard accepts the token, the tool reads current modes with `GET /v1/service`, walks a rung at a time, then **reads the services back** and reports `applied` only for what the controller actually holds. If something did not land it raises `UpstreamError` naming the real state, because a 200 from this endpoint is not evidence.
- A service already at the target contributes no intermediate step, so re-applying `Protect` never dips through `Monitor`. Everything already at target → no `PATCH` at all.
- Unknown service names are caught by the read and refused before any write.
- `nv_set_group_policy_mode` hits the same endpoint and had defect 2 too; it uses the same helpers now.

## Breaking change

`scope` is gone. A caller still passing it now fails loudly. That is the point: the only value that ever did anything was the default, and `scope='profile'` was a silent no-op for the entire life of 1.1.0.

## Testing

Tests use a new `conftest.FakeServices` stand-in that reproduces the controller's discard-a-two-rung-jump behaviour — a `respond(200, json={})` mock cannot catch any of this, which is why the original tests passed against broken code. The two tests that encoded the scope→route model are replaced.

Not yet exercised against the live controller — that needs a rebuilt image, and the deployed pod still runs 1.1.0. Spec corrected in Appendix B, PART-C and PART-D.

---
name: service-config-profile-route-is-a-noop
description: "nv_set_service_mode cannot set profile_mode at all; the dimension is chosen by the payload field, not the route, and mode transitions must be stepwise"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: eb3930a1-0e01-40a3-995b-e91d8c7083df
  modified: 2026-07-31T16:48:18.321Z
---

Established against the live 5.6.0 controller on 2026-07-31, by direct
`X-Auth-Apikey` calls from inside the neuvector-mcp pod. Three separate defects
in shipped 1.1.0's `nv_set_service_mode`:

**1. The scope→route model is wrong.** Upstream `RESTServiceBatchConfig` has
FIVE fields, not four — `services`, `policy_mode`, **`profile_mode`**,
`baseline_profile`, `not_scored`. Appendix B omits `profile_mode`. The dimension
is chosen by the *payload field*, not by the path. Proven: `PATCH
/v1/service/config` with `{"config":{"services":[...],"profile_mode":"Monitor"}}`
moves `profile_mode` and leaves `policy_mode` untouched. Measured route
behaviour: `/v1/service/config` works; `/v1/service/config/network` works with
`policy_mode`; `/v1/service/config/profile` is **inert** — moves nothing, on any
field. Since the tool exposes no `profile_mode` argument, no shipped tool in
1.1.0 can set profile enforcement at all (`nv_update_process_profile` has only
entries / `alert_disabled` / `hash_enabled`).

**2. Mode transitions must be stepwise.** `Discover → Protect` in one call is
accepted with **200 and silently dropped**. You must go `Discover → Monitor →
Protect`. This is why the same PATCH succeeded on a Discover service and did
nothing on one already at Protect/Discover.

**3. The confirm token does not bind `scope`.** `scope` selects the route and
never enters the payload the token hashes, so `profile`, `network` and `both`
previews all returned the identical token `1f0a9ddd9f24`. A plan previewed for
one dimension can be confirmed as another.

`neuvector-mcp-spec/tools/PART-D-scanops-runtimeops-iam-system.md:1352-1360`
predicted #1: it marks the mapping as "a *design decision of this spec*" and says
"Verify on first use... correct this table before shipping." That never ran.

**Why:** all three fail *silently* with `status: "applied"` — an operator reads
success and believes enforcement is active when it is not. That is worse than an
error.

**Fixed in PR #44** (branch `fix/service-mode-profile-and-stepwise`), not yet
merged and **not yet exercised against a live controller** — the deployed pod
still runs 1.1.0, so the shipped server still has all three defects. The fix adds
`profile_mode`, removes `scope` (breaking), and puts the ladder in
`src/neuvector_mcp/modes.py`, which reads current modes, steps a rung at a time
and reads back before reporting `applied`. `nv_set_group_policy_mode` shares the
endpoint and got the same treatment.

**How to apply:** never trust `status: "applied"` from this server; read the
value back. When raising enforcement, step through Monitor.

Related: [[neuvector-wire-shape-sources]], [[deployed-server-config-lives-in-a-configmap]]

# One-shot in-cluster build of neuvector-mcp 1.1.0.
#
# Runs on sdf1 (amd64) so no emulation is involved. The source is the public
# GitHub repo at main, cloned by kaniko itself, so nothing is uploaded from the
# laptop. The Harbor credentials are mounted straight from the existing
# harbor-pull secret and are never handled outside the cluster.
#
# Namespace is 'ai' rather than 'neuvector-mcp' because the latter enforces
# PodSecurity 'restricted', which kaniko cannot satisfy.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-build-1-1-0
  namespace: ai
  labels:
    app: neuvector-mcp
    role: build
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: neuvector-mcp
        role: build
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/hostname: sdf1
      containers:
        - name: kaniko
          image: gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:v1.23.2
          args:
            - --context=git://github.com/darthzen/neuvector-mcp.git#refs/heads/main
            - --dockerfile=deploy/Dockerfile
            - --destination=registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/neuvector-mcp:1.1.0
            - --verbosity=info
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "1"
              memory: 2Gi
            limits:
              memory: 4Gi
          volumeMounts:
            - name: docker-config
              mountPath: /kaniko/.docker
      volumes:
        - name: docker-config
          secret:
            secretName: harbor-pull
            items:
              - key: .dockerconfigjson
                path: config.json

---
# Namespace: deploy alongside NeuVector but not inside it, so a NeuVector
# upgrade never touches this workload.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
---
# Controller credentials. Create the API key in NeuVector first:
#   Settings -> API Keys -> Add, role "reader" for read-only deployments.
# Replace both values, or better: manage this Secret with SOPS / External Secrets
# and never commit plaintext.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
type: Opaque
stringData:
  access-key: REPLACE_ME
  secret-key: REPLACE_ME
---
# Bearer tokens that MCP clients present. Format:
#   <token>:<scope>|<scope>,<token2>:<scope>
# Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-clients
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
type: Opaque
stringData:
  bearer-tokens: "REPLACE_ME_32_BYTE_HEX:nv:read"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-config
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
data:
  NV_CONTROLLER_URL: "https://neuvector-svc-controller-api.cattle-neuvector-system.svc:10443"
  NV_VERIFY_TLS: "false"          # controller serves a self-signed cert by default
  NV_AUTH_MODE: "apikey"
  NV_TRANSPORT: "http"
  NV_HTTP_PATH: "/mcp"
  NV_READ_ONLY: "true"
  NV_TOOLSETS: "inventory,vulnerability,compliance,events,policy_read"
  NV_REQUIRE_CONFIRM_TOKEN: "true"
  NV_MAX_ITEMS: "200"
  NV_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS: "60000"
  NV_LOG_LEVEL: "INFO"
  NV_LOG_FORMAT: "json"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: server
          image: localhost:5000/neuvector-mcp:1.1.0
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: neuvector-mcp-config
          env:
            - name: NV_API_ACCESS_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
                  key: access-key
            - name: NV_API_SECRET_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
                  key: secret-key
            - name: NV_HTTP_BEARER_TOKENS
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-clients
                  key: bearer-tokens
          ports:
            - name: mcp
              containerPort: 8080
          # The MCP endpoint requires a bearer token, so an unauthenticated HTTP
          # probe would always fail. Probe the socket instead.
          startupProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: mcp }
            failureThreshold: 30
            periodSeconds: 2
          livenessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: mcp }
            periodSeconds: 20
          readinessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: mcp }
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi }
            limits:   { cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi }
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
  ports:
    - name: mcp
      port: 8080
      targetPort: mcp
---
# Egress to the controller and DNS only. Nothing else, in or out.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  ingress:
    - ports:
        - port: 8080
          protocol: TCP
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: cattle-neuvector-system
      ports:
        - port: 10443
          protocol: TCP
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
      ports:
        - port: 53
          protocol: UDP
        - port: 53
          protocol: TCP
